# **cts-marketing-homepage-design-prompt**

## **CTS Marketing Homepage — In-Depth Design Prompt**

**Project:** Challenging Teenage Sons (CTS) — Dr. Mark Schillinger **Artifact:** Single-page marketing homepage design brief + build prompt **Version:** 1.0 · September 2026 **Use it as:** the complete prompt for generating, rebuilding, extending, or QA-ing this design in any AI design or coding tool. Paste the whole thing, then add your specific ask at the bottom (e.g. "now add a Programmes page in this same system").

### **01 · The one-paragraph brief**

Build a single-page marketing homepage for **Challenging Teenage Sons**, the family mentoring practice of **Dr. Mark Schillinger, PhD — Family Mentor**. The page must feel like **a calm, capable man sitting across the table from an exhausted parent**: editorial and confident rather than clinical, warm rather than salesy. The visual language is **uppercase condensed display type (Bebas) paired with a serif reading face (DM Serif Text)**, on a **deep navy + warm copper/gold** palette over a warm off-white. Every section carries one idea, one headline, one next step. The page's job is to move a parent from *"I'm failing"* to *"there's a method, and there's a man who walks it with families"* — and to get them to **book a free 20-minute call**.

**Mood words:** steady · earned · ancestral · editorial · unhurried · masculine-quiet. **Anti-moods:** wellness-soft, tech-startup gradient, medical/clinical, hype-marketing, countdown-timer urgency.

### **02 · Brand context (do not invent beyond this)**

**Fact**

**Value**

Organization

Challenging Teenage Sons (CTS)

Mark Schillinger, PhD

Title

**Family Mentor** — never "therapist", "coach", or "parent educator"

Sister organization

Young Men's Ultimate Weekend (YMUW), nonprofit rite-of-passage weekend, founded 2000, 200+ young men at the first event

Credibility

Featured on CNN's *This Is Life with Lisa Ling* (2020); interviewed by Katie Couric; 25+ years; referenced in *The Boy Crisis*

Website

[challengingteenagesons.com](http://challengingteenagesons.com)

Booking entry point

The free 20-minute call (

<https://cts.drmarkmentor.com/20-min-opt-in>

)

Motto

*"When families follow the same Way, they don't go astray — they evolve together, every day."*

Central promise

**Stop Parenting. Start Mentoring.**

His family today

Wife Suzanne (now teaches workshops with him), son Gabe (42), daughter Becca — "the happiest divorced-married family in the world"

**The framework the page must express**

**The Compass — R.I.G.H.T. virtues:** Respect · Intelligence · Grace · Humor · True. A shared moral language for the whole family.

**The Roadmap — 12 destinations, all beginning with "Re-":** Reality, Reorientation, Relaxation, Responding, Realization, Revealing, Regulation, Reconciliation, Restoring, Resourcing, Rejuvenation, Renovation.

**The three root causes of family problems:** missing rite of passage · no village of mentors · no "way" of parenting to follow.

**The mentor/therapist distinction:** *"A therapist helps people process the past. A family mentor helps families move forward first."*

**Consequences vs. punishments:** *"Consequences restore integrity. Punishments create polarity."* Delivered **calmly, clearly, compassionately**. The 5 C's: Calmness · Clarity · Brevity · Certainty · Compassion.

**Both/And Principle:** two things can be true at once — the antidote to black-and-white family conflict.

> **Hard rule:** never coin a new named framework, principle, or "law". Only the documented names above exist. If a teaching needs a name that isn't in this list, describe the practice plainly with no label.

### **03 · Audience & emotional target**

**Who is reading:** a parent (usually 38–58) of a boy roughly 12–22, at 10pm, having just had another fight that went nowhere. Common reality: the son is in his room with a screen, unmotivated, disrespectful, or 20 and not launching. The parent is exhausted, secretly ashamed, and afraid of being a bad parent. Many arrive carrying something heavier: cutting, suicidal talk, substance use, school refusal.

**What they must feel in the first 5 seconds:** *someone finally knows exactly what my house is like, and this person is not going to lecture me*.**What they must believe by the end:** parents are good people who were never given a method; there is a method; this man has walked it with his own family first; a 20-minute conversation costs nothing and might change the year.

**Copy must never:** blame parents, shame sons, use "toxic masculinity", frame therapy as the answer, or offer generic reassurance ("you're doing great!"). **Copy must always:** name the pain specifically, reframe without judgment, and land one concrete next step.

### **04 · Design system — exact tokens**

Define everything once as CSS custom properties; components consume tokens only. **Never hardcode a hex or a Tailwind color utility in a component.**

:root { --background: oklch(0.985 0.006 78); /* warm off-white page */ --foreground: oklch(0.22 0.009 270); /* near-black ink, slight blue */ --primary: oklch(0.34 0.076 252); /* BRAND NAVY — the anchor */ --primary-foreground: oklch(1 0 0); --secondary: oklch(0.93 0.022 248); --muted: oklch(0.96 0.014 77); --muted-foreground: oklch(0.49 0.012 270); --accent: oklch(0.63 0.102 45); /* COPPER — CTAs, numbers, rules */ --accent-foreground: oklch(1 0 0); --border: oklch(0.88 0.014 75); /* warm hairline */ --ring: oklch(0.57 0.085 247); --card: oklch(1 0 0); --brand: oklch(0.34 0.076 252); /* aliases of primary */ --copper: oklch(0.63 0.102 45); --gold: oklch(0.75 0.092 77); /* eyebrows on navy, quote marks */ --mist: oklch(0.94 0.025 248); /* pale blue section band */ --soft-ink: oklch(0.36 0.008 270); --radius: 0.5rem; }

​

**Surface rhythm (the page alternates so it never reads flat):**

white header → navy hero (photo) → navy method → mist roadmap → navy testimonial → mist contact → navy footer.

**Color law:** navy and copper are the brand. Gold appears only as a small accent on navy. Never introduce a new hue; a new page must be assembled from these surfaces only.

### **08 · Page blueprint — sections, in order, with exact copy**

**1. Hero**

Full-bleed photograph of a father and teenage son talking at home,

object-fit: cover

,

min-height: min(730px, calc(100svh - 76px))

, content vertically centered. A directional scrim sits over it:

linear-gradient(90deg, navy 87% → navy 57% at 43% → transparent at 80%)

, so the left column is readable and the faces stay visible on the right.

Eyebrow: **For parents of teenage boys** (gold)

H1: **You haven't *lost* him.** / **There's a way back.** — "lost" in copper, line break after the first sentence

Body (max 560px, 21px serif): *If your son has retreated into his screen, his room, or himself — you're not failing. You just haven't been given a way. I'll show you one that works.*

Actions:

Book a free 20-min call

Take the assessment

**2. The Method (navy)**

Eyebrow **The method** (gold) → H2 **A compass, not a curriculum.** → serif 20px intro: *Most parents are improvising. The RIGHT Way gives your whole family one shared language for what matters — and a 12-destination roadmap to walk it together.*

Mentor strip: 64px circular portrait, then

Dr. Mark Schillinger

**01 Stop parenting.** — *Reacting, nagging, and punishing train him to tune you out.*

**02 Start mentoring.** — *Guiding, holding steady, and letting consequences teach.*

**03 Walk the RIGHT Way.** — *Respect · Intelligence · Grace · Humor · True. Together.*

**3. The Roadmap (mist)**

Eyebrow **The 12-destination roadmap** → H2 **Every family I work with walks the same path, in their own time.**

A 385px-tall full-width editorial image (families around a table), 7px radius.

The 12 destination cards in a **4 × 3 grid**, 14px gutters, in this fixed order: Reality, Reorientation, Relaxation, Responding, Realization, Revealing, Regulation, Reconciliation, Restoring, Resourcing, Rejuvenation, Renovation.

Copy rule for destination descriptions (if expanded): name the destination plainly, never sell it. Reconciliation = consequences without yelling. Restoring = the in-home rite of passage (Separation → Transition → Integration). Renovation = the empty nest, and a life waiting for the parents.

**4. Testimonial (navy)**

Now we spend our time in laughter, discussion, and creative pursuits. It's like having a training manual on how to raise a teenage son.* Attributed in Bebas 17px gold uppercase, non-italic: **The Rodriguez Family**.

**5. Contact (mist, id="contact")**

Left: H2 **Let's talk for *twenty minutes.*** ("twenty minutes" in copper), serif intro *No pitch. No pressure. Tell me what's happening with your son — and I'll tell you honestly if I can help.*, then accent CTA **Book your free call →**.

Right: white bordered "What to expect" panel — 01 A real conversation, not a questionnaire · 02 An honest read on where your family is · 03 Clarity on whether my method fits you · 04 Zero pressure to decide anything today.

True, Dr. Mark · Family Mentor

[challengingteenagesons.com](http://challengingteenagesons.com)

**Sign-off law:** any long-form text on this brand ends **True, Dr. Mark** — with a P.S. carrying the soft CTA when it's an email.

### **09 · Responsive behavior**

Two breakpoints only.

**≤900px:** hide nav + header CTA, show hamburger; footer grid → 2 columns; contact gap tightens to 35px.

**≤650px:** header 66px; hero switches from centered to

align-items: flex-end

 with a **bottom-up** scrim (

96% → 78% at 50% → 6%

) and

object-position: 67% center

 so the faces stay in frame above the fold; H1 drops to

clamp(49px, 11vw, 70px)

; buttons 47px/17px; pillars stack to 1 column; destination grid → 2 columns with 24px titles; testimonial and contact become single column; footer brand cell spans full width and the bottom bar stacks.

Nothing may horizontally scroll at 320px, and no destination name may clip (

overflow-wrap: anywhere

 is already on card titles).

### **10 · Motion & interaction**

The page's personality is **restraint**. Nothing bounces.

Smooth scroll for in-page anchors;

scroll-behavior: auto

 under

prefers-reduced-motion

.

Card hover: 200ms

translateY(-3px)

 + copper border + soft shadow. Nothing scales.

Buttons: 150–200ms background/border/color transition only.

Header stays solid white and sticky; no blur, no shrink-on-scroll.

If scroll reveals are added, keep them to a 400–500ms fade + 12px rise, once, and disable them entirely under

prefers-reduced-motion

 (which must collapse all transition/animation durations to ~0).

### **11 · Accessibility**

Landmarks:

<header>

,

<main id="top">

,

<footer>

; each section labelled by its heading via

aria-labelledby

; the navs carry

aria-label

.

Every heading level descends in order (one h1, section h2s, card h3s).

Text on the hero photo must clear 4.5:1 — that's what the scrim is for; verify, don't assume.

Hamburger exposes

aria-expanded

 and swaps its label between "Open menu" and "Close menu"; it is a real

<button>

.

Visible focus ring from

-ring

; keyboard tab order matches visual order; the mobile menu closes when a link is chosen.

Decorative marks (the CTS block in the footer, the quote glyph) are

aria-hidden

.

Reduced motion respected; no auto-playing anything.

### **12 · Art direction for imagery**

Four editorial photographs, local files, real imports — no stock-photo gloss, no smiling-to-camera family poses.

**hero-family** (1536×1024) — father and teenage son in conversation at home, natural window light, muted palette, the son not performing happiness. Must be readable under a navy scrim from the left.

**workshop** (1536×1024) — families gathered around a table mid-conversation; documentary, not a boardroom.

**mentor** (768×768) — a portrait that reads as a calm, experienced man in his 60s; will be shown as a 64px circle, so it must hold up small.

**testimonial** (768×768) — a mother and teenage son, warm, unposed.

Grade all four consistently: warm shadows, low saturation, no teal-and-orange, no lens flare. Photos are the only "soft" element on the page; the chrome stays sharp.

### **14 · Guardrails — things this design must never do**

Never invent a named framework, principle, or statistic. Use only the RIGHT Way Method, Both/And Principle, the 12 destinations, the 5 C's, and the Compass virtues.

Never blame or shame a parent, and never describe the son as a bad kid — *"90% of the sons I mentor are really great dudes."*

No purple/indigo gradients, no glassmorphism, no emoji in the interface, no rounded-2xl everywhere, no default Inter-as-identity.

No fake scarcity: no countdown timers, no "only 3 spots left", no pop-up modals on load.

No stock imagery of a family high-fiving; no therapists' office imagery.

Don't call Dr. Mark a therapist, coach, guru, or expert — he is a **Family Mentor**.

Don't add a section unless it earns its place; the current six are the whole argument. One idea per section.

Keep the tone calm authority — never panicked, never salesy, never cute.

### **15 · Definition of done (QA checklist)**

Desktop 1280 and mobile 390 screenshots show no overflow, clipping, or overlap.

Hero headline breaks as designed on both; the faces sit clear of the scrim and the CTA.

All 12 destinations render in exact order, none truncated, 4-up desktop / 2-up mobile.

Pillar numerals read as display type (~54px) — verify computed styles, not just the CSS.

Every button is a real pill, uppercase Bebas, and its hover state is visible.

Mobile menu opens, closes on selection, and announces

aria-expanded

 correctly.

Keyboard-only pass reaches every CTA; focus is always visible.

Text over the hero photo passes 4.5:1.

No console or build errors; fonts load with

font-display: swap

; LCP image is the hero and is not

loading="lazy"

.

Every CTA that should book actually reaches the booking URL.

### **16 · Open items to resolve before launch**

Booking links currently point at

[challengingteenagesons.com](http://challengingteenagesons.com)

 and in-page anchors; they should route to the real 20-minute call scheduler.

The four photographs are placeholders and must be replaced with real portraits of Dr. Mark and real family photography (with permission).

"Take the assessment" is not yet a live assessment experience — it needs its own route and flow.

Newsletter/social proof and a podcast route can be added later in this same system; nothing new should be added without the six sections' rhythm staying intact.
